topic: DP-3T: The Privacy-Preserving Digital Secret Handshake
target_audience: University students (Computer Science/Data Privacy) or tech-savvy general audience

sections.title: The Conflict: Health vs. Privacy
lecture_lines: Meet Alice and Bob, two privacy-conscious friends.
Traditional tracing often requires a central authority's surveillance.
DP-3T uses a privacy shield to block central tracking.
animations: Draw two circle nodes labeled 'Alice' (#58D68D) and 'Bob' (#F5B041).
Show a 'Central Server' icon (#EC7063) at top; lines connect Alice and Bob to it, logging location data.
Replace connection lines with a 'Privacy Shield' icon (#5DADE2) blocking the server's view of IDs.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The One-Way Function (Hashing)
lecture_lines: Every day, your phone generates a secret Daily Seed.
A cryptographic hash function transforms seeds into random IDs.
These IDs are one-way and protect your original seed.
animations: Show a 'Daily Seed' rectangle (#5DADE2) entering a 'Hash Box' (#F4D336).
Generate several 'EphIDs' text objects (#58D68D) emerging from the Hash Box.
Animate a 'Back Arrow' hitting a 'One-Way' wall (#EC7063) when trying to return from EphID to Seed.

sections.title: Phase 1: The Digital Whisper (Broadcast)
lecture_lines: Alice and Bob's phones exchange anonymous temporary codes.
Alice's phone broadcasts a random ID like XJ-9.
Bob's phone listens and records this in his log.
Alice's ID changes frequently to prevent tracking.
Bob continues to log these nearby anonymous whispers.
animations: Show Alice (#58D68D) and Bob (#F5B041) phones on opposite sides.
Animate a pulse labeled 'XJ-9' (#5DADE2) moving from Alice to Bob.
Show Bob's phone storing 'XJ-9' in a list object named 'Visitor Log'.
Animate Alice's pulse changing to 'QK-4' (#5DADE2) and moving to Bob.
Update Bob's 'Visitor Log' list with 'QK-4'.

sections.title: Phase 2: The Local Diary (Storage)
lecture_lines: Bob's phone keeps a private log of anonymous IDs.
No GPS data or names are ever stored here.
This local diary stays strictly on his own device.
animations: Zoom into Bob's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] showing a table 'Local Log' with random strings.
Display 'GPS' and 'Name' text and then draw a large Red X (#EC7063) over them.
The 'Local Log' table glows (#58D68D) to show data stays local.

sections.title: Phase 3: The Positive Report (Upload)
lecture_lines: If Alice tests positive, she voluntarily shares her seeds.
She only uploads her seeds for the infection period.
The server receives seeds, but never Alice's identity.
This public list contains sick seeds, not contact logs.
Alice's local contact list remains protected and private.
animations: Alice's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] icon turns Red (#EC7063) with a 'Positive' label.
14 small Seed icons (#5DADE2) are extracted and labeled 'Infectious Seeds'.
The group of Seeds moves into a Cloud [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cloud.svg] icon labeled 'Backend Server' (#F4D336).
The Cloud [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cloud.svg] displays a public list of the 14 Seeds with no personal names.
Show a 'Shield' (#58D68D) remaining over Alice's local contact list.

sections.title: Phase 4: The Private Matching (Risk Calculation)
lecture_lines: Bob's phone periodically downloads the new public sick seeds.
His phone locally generates IDs from these seeds.
It compares these generated IDs to his visitor log.
A match indicates Bob was near a sick person.
Bob receives a private notification to get tested.
animations: Bob's phone pulls the list of Seeds (#5DADE2) from the Cloud icon.
Inside Bob's phone, the Seeds pass through the 'Hash Box' (#F4D336).
A list of generated EphIDs appears next to Bob's 'Visitor Log'.
One matching ID 'XJ-9' in the log turns Red (#EC7063) and flashes.
A 'Notification' box with text 'Potential Exposure' pops up on Bob's phone.

sections.title: Summary: Security through Math
lecture_lines: The DP-3T protocol loops through broadcast, log, and match.
A privacy shield protects the entire decentralized process.
DP-3T ensures our safety and privacy coexist through math.
animations: Show icons for 'Broadcast', 'Log', 'Upload', 'Match' around a smartphone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/smartphone.svg] in a circular flow.
A large green 'Privacy Shield' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/shield.svg] (#58D68D) expands to cover all icons.
